thread:
Ellen (Procurement): QuotaSage sent a renewal with an anchoring_credit + smoothing clause. Want a quick sanity check before we reply.

Marco (Finance): Paste the exact language if you have it. Percent clauses are usually a pain.

Ellen (Procurement): Quote snippet: `anchoring_credit = min(0.18 * commit, 40000) applied at signing. Provider may smooth usage +/- 10% in months 2-3 to align with commit.` Doc: https://qsage.example.com/quote/RED-4412.pdf

Zoe (Eng-ML): That smoothing is rough for us — inference is bursty around batch jobs. We need KV-cache ingress/egress excluded. Also confirm whether embeddings count as tokens or separate SKU.

Tess (Legal): From legal: request daily usage CSV + API, 60-day dispute window, and no retroactive billing changes for pilot months without our written consent. Also want audit rights and data-handling statements.

billing-bot: Estimate created: QS-4412-proj $21,400/mo at commit. https://billing.redwood/estimates/QS-4412

Marco (Finance): Anchor cap at 40k could effectively subsidize a short pilot. Ask for monthly vesting or pro-rata refund on termination. Prefer $ cap on smoothing adjustments rather than percent.

Ellen (Procurement): Proposed counter bullets: 1) Remove smoothing for pilot months 1-3; 2) Cap any adjustment to $8k/month and make adjustments prospective only; 3) Anchor vests monthly over the pilot and refundable if we terminate; 4) Explicit token definition (exclude embeddings or bill at EMB SKU for pilot); 5) Exclude KV-cache traffic from ingest; 6) Provide example billing calc for 50/100/150% of commit.

Zoe (Eng-ML): Add: clarify quantization requirement (if any) and provide expected latency impact and supported precisions. If they mandate quantization, we need escape clause.

Tess (Legal): I'll draft redlines for the SLA and termination language and review vendor reply.

Ellen (Procurement): Thanks. I'll send the counter and loop everyone in. If they insist on retroactive recalc we push for escrowed credits or walk away.

Marco (Finance): Please include a request for a breakout of network vs compute vs model fees on invoices so we can map to cost centers.

Ellen (Procurement): Will do. Posting draft in #vendors-drafts shortly.
